title: Prime a steel plate with a block brush: wipe it off on the tray rim, re-dip as it runs dry
instruction: Give the steel plate a coat of primer.
context: Before fabricated steel is assembled it gets a coat of primer, brushed on from a tray. A painter loads the brush, wipes the excess off on the tray's rim so it does not drip across the shop, and re-dips when it runs dry, until the whole plate is covered. The instruction mentions neither the brush, the tray nor the wiping.
setup: Bare steel plate (120 x 70 x 8 mm, fixed) at (0.33, 0). Paint tray (70 x 100 mm inside, 16 mm deep) of red-oxide primer, 10 mm deep, at (0.33, 0.175). Block brush (70 x 16 mm pale bristle head, 110 mm round wooden handle, 60 g) lying bristles-down at (0.22, 0.20), handle toward the arms.
scoring: Coverage is the fraction of the plate's 84 10-mm patches with primer on them. 0.25 at 30%, 0.5 at 60%, 0.75 at 95% with at most 1 drip of primer on the bench and no primer brushed onto the bench (loaded bristles flat on it off the plate and tray). 1.0 adds the brush then put down flat off the plate (in the tray or on the bench) and let go, held 1 s. Primer is only applied by a brush loaded in the tray; one dip covers 45 patches, so the plate needs at least two. A brush carried out of the tray without being wiped on the rim drips every 0.2 s.
fidelity: PhysX rigid bodies at 240 Hz. Wet primer is not simulated: from the brush's measured pose, tips sunk in the tray load it with 45 patches; loaded tips flat on the plate coat each 10 mm patch they pass (a drawn tile appears); an unwiped brush outside the tray releases a 7 mm rigid drop every 4 steps. Bristles are one rigid block; plate and tray are fixed.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 after 129 steps (6.45 simulated seconds); termination: DreamSessionExpired:expired. Scripted/teleoperated demo: 1 after 875 steps.
